This is a review for the ground up remake of Resident Evil 2. I got my copy at a local second hand shop for a good price. I personally don’t buy too many games new for clear reasons in the current gaming climate. I don’t want to spend $60 or so on pozzed politically injected garbage.

A beloved game of my personal childhood. Resident Evil 2 was one of my favorites along with Tony Hawk 2, GTA 2, Metal Gear and others. When I played Resident Evil 4 I wished Calvin would do something with 2. For me personally this is a great homage to the original.

Let’s get any pozz out of the way first. I don’t detect much to any in this one. Leon is still white and capable same deal with Claire. There is the police chief who is black but no major attention is drawn to that fact. He even admits he messed up! Zombies are all varieties of people. To me, there doesn’t seem to be much subversion in the games dialogue.

Gameplay is great imo. There are two stories you can play at first. Leon or Claire. Both have overlapping areas but feature different characters and objectives. There are also second runs that let the player see more of Raccon City. The second runs are unlocked in opposite. Claire for Leon and vice versa. Each character has unique weapons. Utilizing these against enemies takes a little trial and error some work better on some enemies than others. For example using the desert eagle styled gun Leon gets against zombies is useless. Save that ammo for Lickers and boss fights. Item and inventory management is a key point to the game again. Wrecklessly using ammo in fights or healing items can leave in the end game in bad situations. It is forgiving to a point but definitely not on hardcore mode. Saving healing items and avoiding fights is a good idea. Saving gunpowder varieties to make certain ammunition types is also a good idea. Typically gun powder plus gun powder yields regular cartridges, higher power gun powder plus gun powder yields shotgun shells and hp plus hp yields magnum rounds. I tend to make shotgun rounds as they are versatile in all situations. Weapon upgrades can also be optained making weapons easier to use and more lethal. These are usually locked behind some kind of puzzle, combination lock or back tracking. I wrote down all the locks combos so in subsequent play throughs I can advance faster. An interesting detail to the guns is when you have it, if you put it in your safe box the empty holster stays on your character. Same deal with your sub weapon. (Flash grenades, grenades and knives.) each of those also has their own unique benefits. Controls wise I found it to be the best of the series. You can strafe fire where in 4 you had to be planted, quick turns are available and you can run or walk as slowly as possible which comes in handy for some enemies that use sound to detect you. At times walking slowly and carefully is the best option. The game itself is rather short. It took me 8 hours to complete the first run for Leon. This is not knowing where to go and getting lost. Second run was a little over 4. The game targets 3:30mins for a “S” ranked run. Doing replays are where the game sets it’s value at. If you don’t like replaying for more rewards you’re looking at maybe a 20hr game tops. There are three modes of difficulty easy, standard and hardcore. I’ve only tested the waters in hardcore. Getting bit once sends you to danger levels of health. There are extra modes called ghost survivors which focus on sub stories of characters you run across in the game. These imo are very tough. I haven’t been able to complete one yet. They are a mix of all different enemies with extreme item management and knowledge of enemies to survive. I enjoy them because they are good tests of what you have learned but they can tax my patience. I’ve spent a few hours messing around with them. There are also records for doing certain things in game that will earn you concept art, models and what I’m going after infinite ammo for certain guns. Some are easy, some hard and some very vague as to what you have to do to complete them. This extends the game for me as well. Graphics wise the game is on par with anything I’ve seen recently. An abundance of gore and shock. Some deaths are pretty brutal. Sound is good although I prefer playing with the music off, no film grain filter and no camera wobble. I find these unnecessary at times and annoying like chromatic aberration that was popular years ago. My opinion.

To the annoying things. Some zombies take 10 or more rounds to destroy a zombie’s brain with 9mm or 45acp. Sometimes it’s one round so it’s hard to tell what’s gonna happen. The unreliability of small arms is a problem for me. Shotguns usually do the trick but sometimes point blank 12 gauge bursts don’t do it. As well if it isn’t destroyed they may suddenly be back walking around again later in the game. They can be set right behind doors so you walk in and bam no time to react at all. The camera can be a bastard at times and gets frustrating to baby sit during boss fights. Bosses can have way more reach than you would expect and manuvering clearly can be almost impossible in tight spaces. Not being able to search areas you have to develop film for is kind of a pain but expected. Even though you can magically know combination locks. The story itself is good and provides some good back story but is kind of shallow imo. Some areas seem to be confusing on purpose mainly the sewers and the maps can be a mess as well. The puzzles are largely fun but can be tedious on multiple play throughs until you memorize them.

I’d say this is a good game around and 8/10 especially if you have played the original. I’d suggest picking it up at sub $30 because that’s about what it’s worth. Replays to me don’t justify $60 price tags.
